## What was wrong

`oneJourneyH` was a literal `70`, and the banner drew at `oneJourneyH - 10`. Every other box on the story map sizes itself with `fitHeight`. Any `one_journey` sentence wrapping past two lines lost its last one — silently, because a tldraw geo draws its overflow outside itself rather than complaining.

On the board that surfaced it: **60px drawn against 112px of text**, and the closing clause was simply not on the page.

Same class as #431 — a dimension asserted rather than measured — found while confirming that fix in an exported image.

## The fix

Hoist the width that was already being computed inline, measure the same string the label will hold, keep the 10px the draw subtracts back.

```js
const oneJourneyW = Math.max(600, steps.length * PITCH - 20)
const oneJourneyH = model.one_journey ? fitHeight(`ONE JOURNEY\n${model.one_journey}`, oneJourneyW) + 10 : 0
```

## Evidence

- **77/77 model tests pass**, up from 75.
- **Boot-and-render smoke passes**: 262 shapes across 5 pages, round trip clean.
- **Rendered and looked at.** The example board exports with the banner intact — the sentence now ends in "kept in the file." instead of stopping mid-clause. Screenshotted and read, not just written.
- **Re-rendered a real 49-story board**: banner went from 60px to 112px against the same text.

Two tests, three mutations, all three fail both tests:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| restore the literal `70` | both fail |
| measure at `oneJourneyW * 3` | both fail |
| drop the `+ 10` the draw subtracts | both fail |

## Why the second test is the one that matters

The targeted test pins this banner. The broad one asserts **no geo on the page is shorter than the text inside it** — and it caught exactly one shape, this one. So the invariant already held everywhere else, and the class is now closed rather than the instance patched. If a future box is added with a guessed height, that test fails before anyone has to notice it in an image.

## without-it unanswered

- The broad test walks `type === 'geo'` with non-empty text. A `note` grows at runtime via `growY`, so notes are out of its reach by construction, not by oversight — but nothing states that anywhere except this sentence.
